Ross）的粉丝们现在可以竞拍他的一幅风景油画了。据拍卖行基特雷尔艺术（Ketterer Kunst）向德新社驻慕尼黑分社透露，罗斯在1986年当着摄像机镜头创作的画作《山间壮丽》（Mountain Splendor）将于5日12月登台拍卖。净收益将用于在国家资金削减后支持美国公共电视台。这幅美国艺术家（1942-1995）的画作估价在40.000至60.000欧元之间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电视播出的绘画课程《绘画的乐趣》（Joy of Painting）真正成为了某种文化现象，罗斯在1983年至1994年期间通过该节目向观众普及油画风景画，尽管其风格多少带有一种媚俗的色彩。他通过赞美“快乐的云朵”或为“快乐的树木”安排伙伴来倾倒粉丝。他对学员们的寄语是：“我们不犯错误，只有快乐的小意外”。学术界甚至创造了“鲍勃·罗斯效应”一词，用来形容其对调节情绪的积极作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "人们可以在第七季第八集中见证《山之壮丽》（Mountain Splendor）的诞生。开头时，这位留着标志性蓬松卷发的美国艺术家站在画布前，用橙色落下了第一笔色彩。在工作的同时，他一边劳作一边进行解释和评述。现场只能听到他那令人安心的声音和画笔沙沙的摩擦声。在大约27分钟后，罗斯在树木上轻柔地点缀出绿色的树叶——画作便完成了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“流行文化偶像”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "和艺术家的其他作品一样，《山之壮丽》（Mountain Splendor）展现了一处柔和色彩中的理想化风景。一座山脉拔地而起，前方是一片湖泊，四周环绕着树木。一切都沐浴在带有秋意般的温和光线之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“鲍勃·罗斯曾激发了数百万人对绘画的热情，并早已成为一个流行文化偶像，”拍卖行老板罗伯特·克特雷尔（Robert Ketterer）说道。该艺术家的YouTube主页和节目拥有超过6,60 million名关注者。在德国，《绘画的乐趣》（Joy of Painting）可以在ARD媒体库以及流媒体服务商Wow等平台找到。", "links": [{"text": "in der ARD Mediathek", "url": "https://www.ardmediathek.de/sendung/bob-ross/Y3JpZDovL2JyLmRlL2Jyb2FkY2FzdFNlcmllcy82YmM4YzFhMS1mYWQxLTRiMmYtOGRjYi0wZjk5YTk4YzU3ZTA"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2019年，美国达拉斯附近的一所学校甚至为罗斯举办了一场快闪活动。艺术专业的学生们戴着巨大的卷发假发，以此向这位艺术家致敬。罗斯于1995年因癌症去世，享年仅52岁，生前创作了超过30 000幅画作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "资金支持美国公共电视", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“通过《山之壮丽》（Mountain Splendor），我们拍卖的不仅是一幅画，还有一段电视历史，”克特雷尔确信道。“我们能够在德国首次提供一件原作，并同时支持美国的公共电视台，这让这场拍卖对我们而言具有特殊意义。”据拍卖行称，节目发行商美国公共电视台（APT）是在一项慈善倡议的框架下提供这幅画作的。起因是美国削减了已经批准的用于公共电视的联邦资金。克特雷尔表示，该公司希望利用包括美国其他类似拍卖在内的资金，来帮助各电视台维持节目的播出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这并不是罗斯的画作第一次被拍卖。基特雷尔表示，1990年的电视画作《季节更替》（Change of Seasons）曾以787.900美元的创纪录价格成交。其他画作也曾大幅超出估价。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Wenn der Künstler Bob Ross im Fernsehen vor laufender Kamera seine Landschaftsgemälde malte und von glücklichen Bäumen schwärmte, sahen die Menschen begeistert zu. Nun ist eines seiner Werke zu haben

Fans des berühmten TV-Malers Bob Ross können nun eines seiner Landschaftsgemälde in Öl ersteigern. Am 5. Dezember komme sein Bild "Mountain Splendor" unter den Hammer, das Ross 1986 vor laufender Kamera gemalt habe, teilte das Auktionshaus Ketterer Kunst der dpa in München mit. Mit dem Nettoerlös würden öffentliche US-Sender nach der Kürzung staatlicher Mittel unterstützt. Auf 40.000 bis 60.000 Euro wird das Gemälde des US-Amerikaners (1942-1995) geschätzt.

Regelrecht Kult wurde der im Fernsehen ausgestrahlte Malkurs "Joy of Painting", in dem Ross zwischen 1983 und 1994 seinem Publikum die Landschaftsmalerei in Öl nahebrachte, wenn auch in einer eher kitschigen Variante. Er bezauberte seine Fans, indem er von "fröhlichen Wolken" schwärmte oder "glücklichen Bäumen" Freunde an die Seite stellte. Seinen Schülerinnen und Schülern gab er mit: "Wir machen keine Fehler, nur glückliche Missgeschicke". Die Wissenschaft sprach gar vom "Bob-Ross-Effekt", der sich positiv auf die Stimmung auswirke.

Die Entstehung von "Mountain Splendor" kann man in Folge acht der siebten Staffel erleben. Zu Beginn steht der US-Künstler mit dem charakteristischen, großen Lockenkopf vor einer Leinwand und setzt erste Farbstriche in Orange. Während er arbeitet, erklärt und kommentiert er seine Arbeit. Nur seine beruhigende Stimme und das kratzende Streichen des Pinsels sind zu hören. Nach rund 27 Minuten tupft Ross zartes, grünes Laub an die Bäume – und das Bild ist fertig.

"Ikone der Popkultur"

"Mountain Splendor" zeigt wie auch andere Werke des Künstlers eine idealisierte Landschaft in sanften Farben. Ein Bergmassiv ragt in die Höhe, davor liegt ein See, umrahmt von Bäumen. Alles ist in ein herbstlich anmutendes mildes Licht getaucht.

"Bob Ross hat Millionen Menschen für die Malerei begeistert und ist längst zu einer Ikone der Popkultur geworden", sagt Robert Ketterer, Inhaber des Auktionshauses. Der YouTube-Seite des Künstlers und der Sendung folgen mehr als 6,6 Millionen Menschen. In Deutschland ist "Joy of Painting" unter anderem in der ARD Mediathek und beim Streaminganbieter Wow zu finden.

2019 gab es an einer Schule in der Nähe von Dallas in den USA sogar einen Flash Mob für Ross. Kunststudentinnen und Kunststudenten erschienen mit riesigen Lockenperücken zu Ehren des Künstlers, der 1995 mit nur 52 Jahren an Krebs gestorben war und mehr als 30 000 Bilder geschaffen hatte.

Geld unterstützt öffentliches US-Fernsehen

"Mit 'Mountain Splendor' versteigern wir ein Stück Fernsehgeschichte", ist Ketterer überzeugt. "Dass wir erstmals ein Original in Deutschland anbieten können und damit zugleich das öffentliche Fernsehen in den USA unterstützen, macht die Auktion für uns besonders." Dem Auktionshaus zufolge bietet der Programmverteiler American Public Television (APT) das Gemälde im Rahmen einer Charity-Initiative an. Anlass sei die Kürzung bereits bewilligter Bundesmittel für das öffentliche Fernsehen in den USA. Mit dem Geld auch aus anderen, ähnlichen Auktionen in den USA will das Unternehmen den Sendern laut Ketterer helfen, das Programm aufrechtzuerhalten.

Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass ein Gemälde von Ross versteigert wird. So sei das TV-Gemälde "Change of Seasons" aus dem Jahr 1990 für den Rekordpreis von 787.900 US-Dollar weggegangen, hieß es von Ketterer. Auch andere Bilder hätten die Schätzpreise deutlich übertroffen.
article_translation_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "當藝術家鲍勃·羅斯在電視上在電視上在電視相機前畫著他的景觀雕像,並從幸運的樹木中滑動時,人們感到興奮。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "著名电视画家鲍勃·罗斯的粉丝现在可以用油来描绘他的景观雕像之一。 5 十二月,他的图像“山 Splendor”在火柴下,Ross 1986 在正在进行的摄像头之前画,拍卖店Ketterer Kunst在慕尼黑的dpa表示,通过净收费,美国公共广播公司将在政府资金削减后支持。 40.000 到 60.000 欧元将成为美国人的形象 (1942-1995) 值得欣赏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在1983年至1994年间,罗斯将景观绘画用油,但在一个更可爱的版本中,在电视上播放的绘画课程“Joy of Painting”,他将他的粉丝欣赏,通过“快乐的云”或“快乐的树木”的友谊,他向他的学生们说:“我们不会犯错,只是快乐的错误。“Bob-Ross效应”,对情绪有积极的影响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“山 Splendor”的起源可以随后体验到第七个季节的八个。 起初,美国艺术家与其特征性的,大尾头站在一堵墙前,并在橙色上放置了第一条颜色线条. 在他工作时,他解释和评论他的工作. 只有他的放松声音和铅笔的尖叫线条可以听到。 约27分钟后,罗斯在树木上打着温柔的,绿色的<unk>子 - 图像已经完成了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“流行文化的标志”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“山 Splendor”与艺术家的其他作品一样,展示了一个理想化的景观,温柔的颜色,一座山脉大楼升高,前面有一座被树木包围的湖泊,一切都沉浸在一个秋天假设的温柔的光线中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“鲍勃·罗斯为绘画感动了数百万人,并在很长一段时间内成为流行文化的图标,”拍卖院的所有者罗伯特·凯特勒(Robert Ketterer)说。 6,6 在德国,“Joy of Painting”在ARD媒体库和流媒体提供商Wow中可以找到。", "links": [{"text": "in der ARD Mediathek", "url": "https://www.ardmediathek.de/sendung/bob-ross/Y3JpZDovL2JyLmRlL2Jyb2FkY2FzdFNlcmllcy82YmM4YzFhMS1mYWQxLTRiMmYtOGRjYi0wZjk5YTk4YzU3ZTA"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2019 在美国达拉斯附近的一所学校,甚至有一张为罗斯的闪光灯泡,艺术学生们以巨大的尾巴珠宝出现在艺术家的荣誉中。 1995 只有 52 多年来,他死于癌症,而且 30 000 他们创造了图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "资金支持美国公共电视", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“与‘Mountain Splendor’我们出售一部电视故事,”Ketterer说,“我们第一次在德国提供一个原创,同时支持美国的公共电视,这对我们来说是特别的拍卖,”拍卖院说,该节目经销商美国公共电视(APT)在慈善倡议的框架内提供这幅画。其他类似的拍卖在美国,该公司希望帮助发行人,据Ketterer说,保持该计划。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是罗斯拍卖的第一张图片,这就是今年的电视画《季节的变化》 1990 以纪录的价格 787.900 美国元已经消失了,据Ketterer称,其他图像也显然超过了估计价格。", "translated": true}]

title_original: Aga Łuczakowska offers a quiet meditation on Ceaușescu’s legacy in Bucharest
editorial_title_zh: 阿加·乌恰科夫斯卡（Aga Łuczakowska）在布加勒斯特带来关于齐奥塞斯库遗产的静谧沉思
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在自出版摄影集《Râsu’-plânsu’》中，阿加·乌恰科夫斯卡审视了在前总统尼古拉·齐奥塞斯库专制政权过去几十年后，布加勒斯特日常生活中低调而微小的细节。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "日常环境中的敏感与象征时刻贯穿了乌恰科夫斯卡的自出版书籍《Râsu’-plânsu’》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗马尼亚语短语“râsu’-plânsu’”（意为“含泪的笑”）描述了在困境中发现温柔、讽刺与韧性的能力。在阿加·乌恰科夫斯卡制作精美的60页平装书中，这个短语与其说是一种历史解释，不如说是一种邀请——它是一场简短而沉浸式的邂逅，带人们以另一种方式去解读地方、记忆以及人们留下的痕迹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Râsu’-plânsu’》并非对前总统尼古拉·齐奥塞斯库强制迁徙和城市化专制计划的详尽记录，而是一场诗意的沉思。在布加勒斯特生活的10年里，乌恰科夫斯卡在上班途中和周末拍摄了这座城市的碎片，让日常生活节奏展现出内置于人造环境中的静谧矛盾。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她的黑白影像超越了独裁政权住宅区宏伟的混凝土结构，发掘出更古老的记忆和个人历史的延续。一条挂在晾衣绳上看似廉价的花卉毯子成了一张平静而深邃的照片，在这粗粝的野兽派现代主义几何结构中，这种俗艳的图案承载着民间传统和乡村想象的回响。其他地方则出现了零星的家居杂物碎片，如盒子、破损的金属制品，这些物件既像是遗失又像是被保存，脆弱却又持久。", "translated": true}, {"type": "quote", "text": "《Râsu’-plânsu’》要求观者慢下来，以不同的视角去观察。它的力量不来自于宏大或完整，而是来自于其观察的亲密感", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乌恰科夫斯卡的作品在其对这些细微、几乎难以察觉的信号的敏感性方面表现卓越。她拍摄的不仅是存在的事物，还有在强加的建筑秩序中适应的痕迹。作为一本安静、低调的书，《Râsu’-plânsu’》要求观者慢下来，以不同的视角去观察。它的力量不来自于宏大或完整，而是来自于其观察的亲密感，这些观察揭示了记忆、身份和人类的韧性如何在旨在改变它们的空间中持续存在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对这一基本前提进行了巧妙的转换，乌恰科夫斯卡还邀请艺术家们对她的出版物进行改编，邀请他们添加绘画或页面，或者剪裁现有的图像。通过允许项目超越她的作者身份进行扩展，她将这个进行中的项目命名为《Râsu’-plânsu’ Interventions》，拥抱了一种权力的去中心化——一种反威权主义——甚至延伸到了她自己的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿加·乌恰科夫斯卡（Aga Łuczakowska）的《Râsu’-plânsu’》为自出版，售价30欧元。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "agaluczakowska.com", "links": [{"text": "agaluczakowska.com", "url": "https://www.agaluczakowska.com/"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
Moments of sensitivity and symbolism in the everyday environment infuse Łuczakowska’s self-published book, Râsu’-plânsu’

The Romanian phrase râsu’-plânsu’ (‘laughing through tears’) describes the ability to discover moments of tenderness, irony and resilience within hardship. In Aga Łuczakowska’s beautifully produced 60-page softback, the phrase becomes less historical explanation and more invitation – a brief, immersive encounter with a different way of reading place, memory and the traces people leave behind.

Rather than offering an exhaustive account of former president Nicolae Ceaușescu’s dictatorial programme of forced relocation and urbanisation, Râsu’-plânsu’ operates as a poetic meditation. Across a decade living in Bucharest, Łuczakowska photographed fragments of the city on her way to work and during weekends, allowing the rhythm of everyday life to reveal the quiet contradictions embedded within the built environment.

Her black-and-white images look beyond the imposing concrete structures of the dictatorship’s housing estates to uncover the persistence of older memories and personal histories. A seemingly cheap floral blanket hanging from a washing line becomes a quietly profound image, the chintzy pattern carrying echoes of folk tradition and a rural imagination within the stark geometry of brutalist modernity. Elsewhere repeated fragments of domestic bric-a-brac appear, boxes, broken metalwork, objects that feel both lost and preserved, brittle yet enduring.

Râsu’-plânsu’ asks the viewer to slow down and look differently. Its power comes not from scale or completeness, but from the intimacy of its observations

Łuczakowska’s work excels in its sensitivity to these small, almost imperceptible signals. She photographs not simply what is present but evidence of adaptation within an imposed architectural order. A quiet, understated book, Râsu’-plânsu’ asks the viewer to slow down and look differently. Its power comes not from scale or completeness, but from the intimacy of its observations, which reveal how memory, identity and human resilience persist within spaces designed to transform them.

In a neat twist on the basic premise, Łuczakowska has also asked artists to adapt her publication, inviting them to add drawings or pages, or cut into existing images. Allowing the project to expand beyond her authorship, she has named this ongoing project Râsu’-plânsu’ Interventions , embracing a decentralisation of power – an anti-authoritarianism – that even extends to her own work.

Râsu’-plânsu’ by Aga Łuczakowska is self-published, priced €30.

article_text:
The death of Eric Bauza in October shocked the entertainment industry. An impressively prolific voice actor, it would’ve been nearly impossible for anybody engaging with animation over the past 15 years to never come across his work. Bauza’s death came just two months after the delayed release of “Coyote vs. Acme,” the “ Looney Tunes ” feature once deemed unreleasable by Warner Bros. Discovery and later sold off to Ketchup Entertainment. The film, which grossed $101 million worldwide, is a true showcase for Bauza, who lends his voice to a plethora of iconic characters, including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety, and Porky Pig.

Bauza became something of the defining voice of modern “Looney Tunes” in his final years. Fans can see him give one final performance with the property in “ Daffy Season ,” a 7-minute animated short that plays before screenings of “The Cat in the Hat,” opening Friday from Skydance’s Warner Bros. Pictures. A representative for the studio confirmed to IndieWire that the short is Bauza’s final “Looney Tunes” movie. Bauza is also credited as providing additional voices for “ The Cat in the Hat .”

“Daffy Season” centers on Daffy Duck, voiced by Bauza. He’s joined by Jeff Bergman as Bugs Bunny, Gabriel Iglesias as Speedy Gonzales, and Jeannie Tirado as Lola Bunny. The plot follows Daffy, turning his beak up at his fellow Tunes as they mindlessly obsess over the game of soccer. Todd Wilderman and Hamish Grieve are co-directors. “Daffy Season” is the first theatrically released “Looney Tunes” short since “Daffy’s Rhapsody” played before “Journey 2: The Mysterious Island” back in 2012.

Before “Daffy Season,” Bauza had already provided some voice work for a “Tunes” musical feature titled “Bye Bye Bunny,” which was canceled after some years of development and production. Other “Looney Tunes” credits from Bauza include the HBO Max series “Looney Tunes Cartoons” and the features “The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie” and “Space Jam: A New Legacy.”

Bauza died at his home in Los Angeles on October 25 as a result of hypertensive cardiovascular disease. A group of organizers have launched a GoFundMe campaign to gather financial support for his son, Ryker Bauza, and Ryker’s mother, Jessica Borutski.

In a tribute in The Hollywood Reporter , Warner Bros. Pictures Animation producer Susan Rogers credited Bauza with playing a huge role in reviving the “Looney Tunes.”

“There wasn’t a single short he couldn’t quote or couldn’t reference,” she said. “I don’t think you replace Eric Bauza … The hole he leaves is huge. There are many talented people out there, and the franchise will move on. But there’s only one Eric Bauza.”
excerpt_original: The new film from Warner Bros. Animation is the first theatrically released "Looney Tunes" short in over a decade.

article_text:
When they were hired to run DC Studios , James Gunn and Peter Safran were tasked with turning the struggling comic book company into a true rival to Marvel. Four years later, the two have been handed their walking papers before they were able to accomplish their task.

Skydance , which recently bought Warner Bros. Discovery and with it the rights to heroes like Superman, Batman, and the other DC staples that Gunn and Safran were trying to reinvigorate, opted to go in another, cheaper direction. They brought in Jeremy Latcham, a low-profile executive who, like Gunn, had spent years working for Marvel, to oversee DC’s latest reboot.

There have been mutterings that the change was because of the commercial performance of DC’s films, and the track record has been a mixed bag. “Superman” did what it needed to do, earning $618.7 million worldwide on a $225 million budget, but it wasn’t a blockbuster on the level of Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” films or “Aquaman.”

But “Supergirl” was an unmitigated disaster , earning $126.5 million against a $170 million budget, resulting in losses of roughly $100 million. And “Clayface,” a body horror film produced for $44 million, has been a modest success, earning approximately $110 million. So no, Gunn and Safran had yet to produce a “Guardians of the Galaxy”-style smash that taps the zeitgeist. Though, to be fair, Marvel hasn’t made as many of those lately either. Tastes have changed, and comic book movies, at least ones not starring Spider-Man , aren’t as popular as they once were.

But look closer, and Gunn and Safran’s ouster is about something more than their films’ commercial performances. It’s about cost-cutting too, something that Skydance, with its $80 billion in net debt, needs to start chipping away at if it’s going to realize the $6 billion in savings it’s promised to find.

The duo’s deal, which was set to expire in 2027, was unusually generous. Safran not only got paid to run the comic book label, he was also allowed to run The Safran Company, the wildly successful production company behind “The Conjuring” franchise (former Netflix film chief Dan Lin, in contrast, divested from his company Rideback when he went over to the streamer). Then there was Gunn, who commanded fees for producing films like “Supergirl” and “Clayface,” as well as fees for those DC films that he wrote and directed, such as “Superman” and “Man of Tomorrow.” Gunn’s total haul for a DC film could be as high as $10 million for all his various duties, according to insiders.

When Warner Bros. Discovery chief David Zaslav offered the pair such a sweet deal, comic book movies looked more durable and he needed to make a splash after DC produced flops like “Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom” and “The Flash.” To sweeten the offer, Zaslav also allowed Gunn and Safran to be relatively autonomous, reporting directly to him, whereas Skydance wanted the DC leadership to be under Skydance Motion Picture Group chiefs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein.

Skydance has also been stunned by the financial picture of Warner Bros.’ film unit since taking over. The studio has suffered a devastating wave of flops this year, losing hundreds of millions on a slate that included bombs such as “Digger,” “The Bride!,” and last weekend’s “The Cat in the Hat.” One insider put the estimated losses at nearing $1 billion. Of course, most of those films were greenlit under Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy, who were let go as soon as David Ellison got the keys to the Warner lot, and have nothing to do with Gunn or Safran. But it does put pressure on Skydance to turn things around and improve the film division’s margins, fast . On an earnings call this week, Ellison acknowledged the film division faces “headwinds” and “has underperformed this year.” He went on to pledge to “apply the same playbook we did at Paramount: greenlighting more selectively.”

Safran remains widely respected on the lot for his stewardship of DC, and is praised for trying to keep budgets in line and for cleaning up the company’s byzantine production practices so that its films, shows, and comic books had a unifying creative voice. Gunn, though a gifted filmmaker, had a harder time adjusting to life in the c-suite, something he admitted to this week in a lengthy post on X. “What only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least,” Gunn wrote. “I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years.” He closed by saying that he was excited to return to working purely as a creator.

Gunn’s habit of engaging with fans directly on social media raised eyebrows at Warner Bros. and, later, at Skydance. But it cut both ways, with Gunn often using his vast following to promote upcoming projects and to engage more directly with fans in a way that inspired loyalty. Insiders also credit Safran and Gunn with not only reinvigorating Superman on screen, but also backing critically acclaimed shows such as “Lanterns” and “Peacemaker.” And the pair handled a delicate situation with the production of “The Batman: Part II,” which was delayed because of personal issues involving its writer and director Matt Reeves, a situation that ultimately required Steven Soderbergh to step in to finish the sequel under Reeves’ guidance . It is expected to wrap production in the next few weeks.

Insiders also note that Gunn and Safran didn’t have a chance to fully realize their vision of making superhero films featuring a wider variety of characters across a greater diversity of genres made for a broader range of budgets. Gunn was already plotting his next move even as he edited “Man of Tomorrow,” which features a team-up of Lex Luthor and Superman. He had outlined a third “Superman” film and was working on a “Justice League” and a “Batman” film, either one of which was expected to be his next project.

In Hollywood, however, timing is everything. And Gunn and Safran had the misfortune of trying to build their own MCU just as comic book movies were declining in popularity. Will Latcham have more success? He’s widely liked and boasts ties to the Christian community that could broaden DC’s core audience. But he also doesn’t come with the kind of pedigree and profile that Gunn did.

As for DC’s fans, they are bracing for yet another reboot having seen the comic book brand they love go through three different regimes over the last decade. Will Latcham provide the kind of consistency the company so desperately needs, or will he be just the latest in a long line of executives asked to pull off a miracle without being granted much of a runway?

article_text:
Ava DuVernay ‘s “14th” will open the 12th edition of San Francisco’s documentary film festival Doc Stories on Nov. 5.

The Netflix film, which premiered at New York Film Festival earlier this month, is one of 10 Oscar-contending feature documentaries included in Doc Stories’ lineup. Others include J.M. Harper’s “Soul Patrol,” Sam Pollard’s “Tutu” and James Marcus Haney’s “Black Sunflowers.”

The four-day festival put on by SFFILM will feature 11 short documentaries, including Joshua Oppenheimer’s “The Revolution Against Death,” about an aging community and its eccentric efforts to achieve immortality, and Oscar winner Laura Poitras ’ “They’re Here,” about ICE agents’ descent on Minneapolis.

Popular on Variety

“For over a decade, Doc Stories has embodied the best of what SFFILM and the San Francisco Bay Area champion and celebrate in new documentary work,” said SFF Film’s executive director Anne Lai, “Each film is a wonderful portal into better understanding the world we live in. When daily life can feel quite bruising and fractious, documentaries skillfully encourage us to let our guard down and connect with real-life stories and people… sometimes challenging, often invigorating, and always meaningful.”

Since its inception, Doc Stories has attracted the who’s who of the nonfiction community. This year, filmmakers including DuVernay, Pollard, Poitras, Luke Lorentzen, and Ben Proudfoot will attend the prestigious Bay Area event, considered the key Oscar season campaign stop in Northern California. Over two dozen Doc Stories selections have earned Academy Award nominations, and several, including “No Other Land” and “Summer of Soul,” have won.

“This year, I found myself drawn to filmmakers who are looking closely at the forces shaping our lives, while also revealing the humor, beauty, resilience, and contradictions within them,” said SFFILM’s director of programming Jessie Fairbanks. “These are documentaries I believe deserve to be seen, talked about, and experienced together — and I’m thrilled to share them with our audiences.”

Running Nov. 5-8 at the Vogue Theatre, the festival will feature three Doc Talks, including a 60-minute conversation with Poitras and her “They’re Here” co-director, Rachel Lauren Mueller. The duo will discuss making “They’re Here” and the challenges they faced while embedding themselves in a Minneapolis community during a wave of ICE raids.

Beyond the public program, SFFILM’s artist development team will convene Doc Congress, a day of dialogue and networking for filmmakers, funders, and industry professionals. This year’s Doc Congress includes a group discussion on AI use in documentaries featuring Srđan Keča, director of Stanford’s MFA in Documentary Film, and Rachel Antell, co-founder of the Archival Producers Alliance. Artist Development will also host an inaugural Pitch Forum for three local filmmakers.

From Nov. 2-10, SFFILM’s Education team will host students and teachers at Schools at Doc Stories, featuring free screenings at SFMOMA, online classroom programs and filmmaker Q&As. The program includes three selections from the main festival, eight additional programs featuring work by Oscar winners Ben Proudfoot and Vanessa Roth, a showcase of films by Berkeley High School students and a teen filmmaking workshop led by Proudfoot. Doc Stories will conclude on Nov. 8.

Opening Night: “14th” THU, NOV 5 AT 6:30 PM PT Ava DuVernay (USA 2026, 107 min) Ava DuVernay examines the enduring promises of the 14th Amendment through a powerful chorus of voices, joining us in person to discuss this vital new documentary.

All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea SAT, NOV 7 AT 5:00 PM PT Jeanie Finlay (UK 2026, 99 min) When a massive sea life die-off threatens his livelihood, lifelong fisherman Stan Rennie rallies his community in a quest for answers, becoming the unlikeliest of activists.

Black Sunflowers

SAT, NOV 7 AT 8:00 PM PT James Marcus Haney (Ukraine 2026, 97 min) Executive produced by Sean Penn, James Marcus Haney’s kinetic, kaleidoscopic portrait of Ukrainian youth is alive with movement, color, and music. Filmed over four years the camera follows artists, drifters, soldiers, and friends as they find pockets of freedom amid mounting uncertainty.

Boatbuilders SUN, NOV 8 AT 4:30 PM PT Luke Lorentzen (USA 2026, 103 min) A visually stunning ode to impeccable craftsmanship and the beauty of Maine, Luke Lorentzen’s latest documentary profiles the workers of Brooklin Boat Yard, a company building custom wooden yachts since 1960.

Citizen Osama SUN, NOV 8 AT 11:30 AM PT Ahmed Hassouna (Palestine, France 2026, 71 min) A photographer turned war reporter documents life in Gaza while raising his newborn son, confronting the impossible challenge of bearing witness to catastrophe while protecting those he loves.

Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been FRI, NOV 6 AT 8:30 PM PT Barry Avrich (Canada 2026, 118 min) The extraordinary singer Darlene Love has lived a big life with its concomitant ups and downs, and this film covers them all as Love herself charts her career, always leading with joy and humor, featuring Cher, David Letterman, Bruce Springsteen, Dionne Warwick, and many more.

Soul Patrol SAT, NOV 7 AT 2:00 PM PT J.M. Harper (USA 2026, 100 min) This moving, creative, and seminal documentary depicts the final reunion of an all-Black six-man patrol team in Vietnam, ensuring that their courage and experiences are not lost to history.

Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing SUN, NOV 8 AT 1:30 PM PT Erik Shirai (Japan, USA, UK, Denmark 2026, 99 min) Erik Shirai cinematically captures the spectacle of strength that is the world of professional sumo wrestling, and shines a rare spotlight on the secrecy of the sport and its formidable competitors.

Closing Night: Tutu SUN, NOV 8 AT 7:30 PM PT Sam Pollard (UK 2026, 102 min) A revelatory portrait of Desmond Tutu, the beloved South African archbishop whose fearless moral voice, infectious humor, and unwavering commitment to justice helped reshape a nation and inspire generations.

Doc Talks: Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller Total Runtime: 60 min SAT, NOV 7 AT 1:30 PM PT Join us for an intimate and candid fireside conversation with filmmakers Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller, who will discuss the challenges they faced while embedding themselves in a Minneapolis community during a wave of ICE raids in their film, They’re Here.

Doc Talks: Jeanie Finlay, Luke Lorentzen, and Erik Shirai Total Runtime: 60 min SAT, NOV 7 AT 3:30 PM PT Doc Talks continues with filmmakers Jeanie Finlay (All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea), Luke Lorentzen (Boatbuilders), and Erik Shirai (Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing), as they discuss the cinematic power of observational storytelling and their unique approaches as both directors and cinematographers.

Doc Talks: Sam Pollard and J.M. Harper Total Runtime: 60 min SUN, NOV 8 AT 2:30 PM PT Doc Talks’ final gathering profiles the esteemed and prolific Sam Pollard and rising star J.M. Harper. Pollard and Harper will discuss their newest features, Tutu and Soul Patrol, and their processes of excavating history, culture, and politics in their work.

Community Screening: Title to Be Announced THU, NOV 5 AT 3:30 PM PT Join us for a community screening of a very special documentary from a notable local Bay Area filmmaker that takes viewers behind the scenes of a major film production. The title of the film will be revealed in late October. Free and open to the public. Attendees must RSVP for tickets at sffilm.org.

Shorts Block: New York Times Op-Docs Total Runtime: 99 min FRI, NOV 6 AT 5:45 PM PT Films are in alphabetical order rather than order of play.

読書好きな中学生3年生の少女・月島雫は、自分が図書館で借りてくる本の貸し出しカードの多くに「天沢聖司」という名前があるのを見つけ、それ以来、顔も知らない天沢聖司の存在が気になっていた。夏休みのある日、図書館に向かう途中で遭遇した一匹のネコに導かれ、雫は「地球屋」という不思議な雑貨店に迷い込む。やがて店主の孫の少年が天沢聖司であることを知り、2人は徐々に距離を縮めていく。しかしバイオリン職人を目指す聖司は、中学を卒業したらイタリアへ渡ることを決めていた。その姿に刺激を受けた雫は、本を読むばかりではなく、自らも物語を生みだそうと決意するが……。 article_text:
耳をすませば（1995）

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

解説・あらすじ

柊あおいの同名少女コミックをスタジオジブリがアニメーション映画化。 読書好きな中学生3年生の少女・月島雫は、自分が図書館で借りてくる本の貸し出しカードの多くに「天沢聖司」という名前があるのを見つけ、それ以来、顔も知らない天沢聖司の存在が気になっていた。夏休みのある日、図書館に向かう途中で遭遇した一匹のネコに導かれ、雫は「地球屋」という不思議な雑貨店に迷い込む。やがて店主の孫の少年が天沢聖司であることを知り、2人は徐々に距離を縮めていく。しかしバイオリン職人を目指す聖司は、中学を卒業したらイタリアへ渡ることを決めていた。その姿に刺激を受けた雫は、本を読むばかりではなく、自らも物語を生みだそうと決意するが……。 宮崎駿や高畑勲の作品を支えてきた名アニメーターの近藤喜文の長編初監督作。98年に46歳で他界した近藤にとって、本作が最初で最後の監督作となった。劇中で雫が生みだす物語世界に、画家でイラストレーターの井上直久が描く架空世界「イバラード」が用いられている。 2026年10月には、スタジオジブリが監修した最高画質の4KデジタルリマスターでIMAX上映。

1995年製作／111分／日本 配給：東宝 劇場公開日：2026年10月23日

その他の公開日：1995年7月15日（日本初公開）

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Jack Champion ( Avatar franchise ) , Owen Patrick Joyner ( Final Destination: Bloodlines) , Grace Van Dien ( Stranger Things ) and Georgie Murphy ( Stumble ) are now leading the YA romance The One Before The One , which Blue Fox Entertainment launched at the Cannes market earlier this year.

Production wrapped in Austin, Texas last month, on the movie written and directed by Brittany Sarkisian, based on a story by John E Clark. The film is produced by Sarkisian and Jaylen Moore for Showmance Productions, along with Raja Collins, Dan Sheldon and Tara Pirnia.

The synopsis reads: “When burned-out Wall Street analyst Steven (Champion) returns to his hometown for his twentieth high school reunion, he is inexplicably transported back to his senior year and reunited with his lost love, Beth (Van Dien). Steven becomes determined to rewrite history, but the version of Beth he spent twenty years idolizing may not be the soulmate he remembered. While trying to ensure his best friend Brian (Joyner) doesn’t once again miss the opportunity to play college football and rebuilding his relationship with his longtime friend and songwriter, Katie (Murphy), Steven slowly comes to realize that the life and love he always wished for might not be the one that got away.”

Watch on Deadline

The film was previously set to star Charlie Gillespie, Sara Waisglass, and Siena Augudong, but scheduling conflicts led to the new cast being drafted in soon over the summer.

The film is said to be “set against the backdrop of late-90s nostalgia: nokia phones, house parties, alt rock, and the looming panic surrounding Y2K”.

Champion is represented by UTA, Amplifed, and Goodman, Genow. Joyner is repped by Prototype Talent Agency, Protégé Entertainment and Myman Greenspan. Murphy is repped by Gersh, Link Entertainment, and Play Management. Van Dien is repped by Innovative Artists and Link Entertainment.

article_text:
News

Paris Students Block Louvre Entrance, Forcing Closure

Students from the independent École du Louvre and the National School of Fine Arts are leading the ongoing action.

Dozens of students from the École du Louvre, a higher education arts institution in the Louvre Palace in Paris, began blocking the main entrance of the Louvre Museum today, October 19, as nationwide protests over the overcrowded and underresourced conditions of France's education system reach the one-month mark.

The blockade prevented the institution from opening at 9 am as students from the grande école, which is located on the museum grounds but operates independently, played music, held up protest art, and distributed leaflets to passersby that read, "We are proud to announce that we are blocking the world's largest museum." Members of the French Democratic Confederation of Labour trade union also stated that students from the National School of Fine Arts are taking part in the demonstration, according to European outlets . The museum did not open today, and it remains unclear whether it will tomorrow.

The Louvre has not replied to Hyperallergic 's immediate request for comment.

article_text:
Con il primo fine settimana di novembre tornano gli appuntamenti dedicati al vintage, al riuso e al collezionismo. Tra mercati ospitati in spazi industriali e manifestazioni nel centro storico, sabato 31 ottobre e domenica 1° novembre offrono diverse occasioni per andare alla ricerca di abiti second hand, vinili, accessori, mobili e oggetti che attraversano epoche e stili differenti. Ecco cinque mercatini da segnare in agenda per il prossimo weekend.

Wunder Mrkt, Milano

Domenica 1° novembre Wunder Mrkt torna negli spazi di Spazio Profumo, l’ex fabbrica di profumi di via Ambrogio Binda 29, a Milano . Il mercato, che ha trovato in questo luogo simbolo dell’archeologia industriale milanese una nuova sede, riunisce oltre cento espositori tra vintage, design, artigianato indipendente e illustrazione.

Accanto agli oggetti di seconda mano e alle proposte creative, la giornata prevede musica, food e occasioni di incontro. L’iniziativa si inserisce in un progetto che mette al centro la cultura del riuso e la possibilità di far convivere produzioni indipendenti e oggetti provenienti da contesti diversi. «Il primo appuntamento ci ha ricordato che non sono i luoghi a creare le comunità, ma le persone a dare vita ai luoghi. Da novembre, la storia continua» L’appuntamento è dalle 11 alle 20:30, con ingresso gratuito.

Mercato delle Pulci, Bologna

Domenica 1° novembre torna sotto la Tettoia Nervi, in piazza Lucio Dalla a Bologna , il Mercato delle Pulci , appuntamento mensile dedicato al riuso. A differenza dei mercati tradizionali dell’antiquariato, la manifestazione coinvolge privati cittadini che mettono in vendita oggetti provenienti dalle proprie case, offrendo una selezione variabile di vestiti, giocattoli, accessori per la casa, mobili, dischi e memorabilia. Il mercato diventa così un’occasione per cercare oggetti di seconda mano, ma anche per dare una nuova destinazione a ciò che non viene più utilizzato. Gli orari di vendita sono dalle 9:30 alle 18.

Verona Antiquaria, Verona

Domenica 1° novembre il quartiere di San Zeno ospita una nuova edizione di Verona Antiquaria, mercato che ogni prima domenica del mese porta nelle strade della zona espositori specializzati in antiquariato, modernariato e collezionismo. Sono oltre duecento gli operatori provenienti dal Nord Italia, con proposte che comprendono mobili, tappeti, oggetti decorativi, vestiti vintage e pezzi d’epoca.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Verona Antiquaria (@veronantiquaria)

Organizzata dall’Associazione Retròbottega in collaborazione con il Comune di Verona, la manifestazione si sviluppa tra piazza San Zeno, piazza Corrubbio e le vie circostanti. La manifestazione vuole includere tutto il quartiere con una proposta tematica che coinvolgerà anche i commercianti di S. Zeno negli allestimenti e nei menù del giorno. L’apertura è prevista dalle 8 alle 17.

Ponte Milvio Antiquariato, Roma

A Roma , domenica 1° novembre, torna anche Ponte Milvio Antiquariato , mercato che si sviluppa lungo via Capoprati, sulle sponde del Tevere, in prossimità dello storico ponte. L’appuntamento riunisce antiquari, rigattieri, collezionisti e artigiani, con un’offerta che comprende oggetti d’arte, arredi, libri, gioielli, accessori e pezzi di modernariato. «Lo scenario dello sfondo, con il verde degli alberi, lo scorrere dell’acqua e la vista di alcuni degli scorci più belli di Roma, rende la manifestazione uno spettacolo unico nel suo genere», si legge sul sito ufficiale della manifestazione. Accanto agli oggetti d’epoca, il mercato permette di esplorare proposte di collezionismo e curiosità provenienti da diversi contesti, in un percorso all’aperto lungo il fiume. L’ingresso è gratuito e l’orario indicato dall’organizzazione è dalle 9 alle 18.

Fiera Antiquaria, Arezzo

«Un viaggio fatto di pezzi rari, favolosi oggetti da collezionare, curiosità e meravigliosi arredi. Un appuntamento con la bellezza dell’antiquariato, del modernariato e del vintage dove potrai fare interessanti scoperte e vivere un weekend inaspettato. E poi c’è la cornice cittadina, con le sue vie brulicanti, i suggestivi scorci medievali, i palazzi e le piazze dall’inconfondibile sapore toscano.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Fiera Antiquaria (@fiera_antiquaria_arezzo)

In occasione della Fiera Antiquaria, Arezzo si veste di un’atmosfera particolare, fatta di storie da ascoltare, persone da conoscere, tesori da scovare e fare propri. Passeggiando per le vie del centro, tra banchi carichi di favolose scoperte, potrai vivere la magia di ritornare bambino. Immergiti nella storia, nei ricordi e nell’infinita bellezza che il passato porta con sé. La Fiera Antiquaria più grande e antica d’Italia ti aspetta ad Arezzo ogni prima domenica del mese e sabato precedente».

La Fiera Antiquaria di Arezzo , appuntamento storico per chi si interessa di antiquariato e collezionismo, si svolgerà quindi anche tra sabato 31 ottobre e domenica 1° novembre, portando nel centro cittadino espositori e oggetti appartenenti a epoche e categorie differenti. Per chi cerca mobili, complementi d’arredo, stampe, ceramiche e curiosità da collezione, la fiera offre l’occasione di esplorare un mercato in cui la ricerca del pezzo particolare si accompagna alla possibilità di confrontare materiali e provenienze.

article_text:
BondIt Media Capital , Buffalo 8 Distribution and Sandaled Kid Productions have partnered on a new slate of horror films.

The partnership will develop three commercial, high-concept horror films. BondIt will finance the slate, while Buffalo 8 will release the titles. Sandaled Kid Productions will focus on development and production of the projects.

“This partnership brings together companies with complementary strengths and a shared belief in bold, commercial genre filmmaking,” James Cullen Bressack, Sandaled Kid Productions founder, said in a statement. “We wanted to build a slate that feels fresh, marketable and genuinely scary, while giving each film the opportunity to stand out in a crowded marketplace.”

Related Stories

Belgian Series 'The Inheritance' Scores Sony Pictures Television Award at Rome’s MIA Market

Sony Pictures Television Hires Lauren Glaubach, Former YouTube and Pinterest Exec, to Lead Digital and Social Distribution Strategy

The deal was negotiated by Bressack and Matthew Helderman, CEO and co-founder of BondIt and Buffalo 8. Bressack and Helderman will both serve as executive producers for the three films.

“James is a longtime collaborator with our teams at both BondIt and Buffalo 8 — and we’re excited for another adventure with him as we target the release of these films for 2027,” Helderman said in a statement. “This genre slate of original films reflects our continued expansion and focus on greenlighting new commercial projects for VOD audiences.”

Additional details, including titles, filmmakers and production schedules, have yet to be announced.

Helderman founded Buffalo 8 in 2010 as an independent media studio focused on production, post-production and distribution. BondIt launched in 2013 with a focus on the eliminating the strain in capital from deposits productions leave with guilds to ensure their members are paid in a timely manner.

Sandaled Kid launched in 2020 with a focus on micro- and mid-budget genre films, particularly action and horror. Bressack’s credits include “Darkness of Man,” “Hot Seat” and “Fortress.”

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Grammy-winning global superstar Raye is coming on to Benny Safdie’s next film Lizard Music to not only voice one of the characters but to also compose original music for the United Artists live-action/CGI hybrid film. She joins previously announced star and producer Dwayne Johnson , Theo Leber, Alicia Silverstone, Tim Heidecker, Arya Parvathi, Regina Hall, Colman Domingo, Jeff Goldblum, Rachel McAdams, David Krumholtz, and Andrew Dice Clay.

The film will be released in theaters December 25, 2027. Safdie wrote the script, which is based on the Daniel Pinkwater novel of the same name.

Related Stories

‘Lizard Music’ Starring Dwayne Johnson And Directed By Benny Safdie To Tune Up Christmas Day 2027 Via Amazon MGM

Alicia Silverstone & Tim Heidecker Latest To Join Benny Safdie’s ‘Lizard Music’

Producers include UA’s Scott Stuber and Nick Nesbitt, Out for the Count Productions’ Benny Safdie, Seven Bucks Productions’ Dwayne Johnson, and Magnetic Fields Entertainment’s David Koplan.

Watch on Deadline

The film will follow a boy (Leber) left to his own devices who stumbles upon a secret late-night broadcast of lizards playing otherworldly music, a hidden door to the extraordinary swings open. His search for answers leads him to an eccentric and whimsical old man nicknamed The Chicken Man (Johnson), and his beloved companion, an 85 year-old chicken named Claudia – the boy and the old man, become two kindred spirits who found each other at just the right time. United by this shared vision, they set off on an adventure that begins as a hunt for a hidden society but blossoms into something far greater: a voyage through invisible worlds, unexpected harmonies, and the unbreakable bond between lost souls who discover magic not only in what they find, but in each other.

Since debuting in 2014, four-time Grammy Award-nominated musician has charted 21 Top 40 UK singles and amassed over 10 billion Spotify streams. In 2024, she made UK music history at the BRIT Awards, winning a record six trophies in a single night and becoming the first woman named Songwriter of the Year, with her debut album My 21st Century Blues taking Album of the Year. Her 2026 sophomore album This Music May Contain Hope won the Mercury Prize, marked her first UK No. 1 album, and debuted Top 10 across 16 territories, highlighting her evolution as an independent artist, songwriter, composer, producer, and arranger.

RELATED: Colman Domingo, Jeff Goldblum, Rachel McAdams & David Krumholtz Join Benny Safdie’s ‘Lizard Music’ In Voice Roles

Closing out 2026 by headlining Spilt Milk festivals across Australia, Raye has just announced This Symphony May Contain Hope. Live From Seven World Wonders , bringing her orchestral production to China, Switzerland, Italy, the US, Australia, and Ghana, with further details to be announced December 10, 2026.

She is represented by Brillstein Entertainment Partners and The Team.

article_text:
IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Video Contest is back, and this year, the prizes are bigger than ever. Anyone interested in attending our intensives at the Cannes International Film Festival, Venice International Film Festival, South by Southwest ( SXSW ), or SXSW London has a chance to win a scholarship to the program of their choice. All you have to do is make an Instagram Reel explaining how the experience would change your life — or if you’re a program alum, explaining how the experience impacted you the first time around and why you’d like to do it again.

The call for entries is now open through Wednesday, December 9, and the winners will be announced on December 22. Videos should be no longer than three minutes in length. Find all the contest details here .

IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Intensives give students and emerging creatives a chance to learn about the industry through attending the world’s greatest film festivals. Participants get to attend major film screenings, panels with filmmakers and industry leaders, networking events, and gain access to an alumni network that follows you for the rest of your career.

Applications for our 2027 programs in Austin, Cannes, London, and Venice are now open (find more info here ). Be sure to apply by the earlybird deadline of November 30.
excerpt_original: A three-minute Instagram reel could be all it takes to attend Cannes, Venice, SXSW, or SXSW London with IndieWire.

article_text:
A planned strike at the V&A over half-term has been suspended after an improved offer from its management.

Museum staff who were members of the Prospect and Public and Commercial Services (PCS) unions had voted to strike on Thursday and Friday in a dispute over pay and working conditions including inadequate toilet and hydration breaks . The strike would have closed the V&A’s main galleries in south Kensington, as well as V&A East, V&A Storehouse and Young V&A in east London.

The strike was suspended on Monday pending last-minute talks with the Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, after the V&A management made an improved offer.

In a statement PCS said it had suspended strikes planned for 29 and 30 October “to allow Acas-facilitated talks to take place, following an improved offer from the museum”. Prospect and the V&A also confirmed the strike had been suspended while negotiations continued.

The unions are demanding a 4% pay increase for staff earning above the living wage, and for the V&A to become an accredited London living-wage employer within 12 months. They also want time-and-a-half pay for bank holiday working.

On conditions, they are seeking improvements to working during heatwaves and better food at the museum’s east London sites. In July, when staff first voted to strike, a V&A spokesperson said “extensive measures” had been introduced to help staff during the heatwave. These included additional rest breaks and closing some galleries during the hottest periods.

The dispute has previously involved two separate two-day strikes in September.

A V&A spokesperson said: “All V&A museums will be open this week, including all exhibitions, free displays and planned half-term activities. While we are working to reinstate as much of our public programme as possible, unfortunately some events may still be cancelled or postponed – visitors are encouraged to check our website before travelling.

“We welcome this opportunity for constructive discussions with our trade union colleagues. Our latest pay offer delivers an average 4.18% pay rise and a 6.9% increase for our lowest-paid colleagues; increased bank holiday pay to 1.5, alongside a sector-leading bonus scheme and a subsidised food offer for staff at all V&A sites.”

Paula Lamont, Prospect’s national secretary, said: “We will be entering talks in good faith and hope that a resolution to the dispute can be found.”

Earlier this month, Prospect’s general secretary, Mike Clancy, called on the V&A’s director, Tristram Hunt, a former Labour MP, to get involved in the negotiations.

He said: “Prospect members are dedicated to their jobs, and it is these dedicated staff who make the museum the world-class attraction it is. That Tristram Hunt can’t even be bothered to take part in the negotiations himself shows the level of disdain in which he holds his staff.”

The London living wage is now £15.45 an hour. While the V&A has said all its staff are paid at least this rate, some of the museum’s outsourced contractors are not. V&A Dundee, which is not involved in the dispute, is an accredited living-wage employer.

article_text:
Siena international photo awards 2026 – in pictures

A selection of some of the awarded photography on display in Siena, Italy, at the festival celebrating the 12th edition of the awards , which runs from 10 October to 29 November

Mon 26 Oct 2026 07.00 EDT

Exhibition: Jasper Doest – Meet Bob

From the passenger seat, the island slides by. One of the things that struck me most while following Bob was how naturally he seemed to move through the rhythms of human life’ Photograph: Jasper Doest/Siena international photo awards 2026

Exhibition: Pierpaolo Mittica – Chernobyl: Memory of a Disaster

Exhibition: Cinzia Canneri – Women’s Bodies as Battlefields

Street photography, highly commended: Varanasi Streets

Animals in their environment, highly commended: Fatal Jump (Kiskunság national park, Hungary)

Animals in their environment, highly commended: Gannets of the Bass Rock (North Sea)

Morus bassanus ) engage in a fast and frenzied hunt for food, tracking shoals of fish from above before plunging into the sea like living missiles at impressive speeds. Their hydrodynamic bodies are equipped with specialised air sacs that protect them from the violent impact with the water. In this feeding frenzy, the birds move together intensely, taking advantage of the abundance of food and competing to grab it first. Bass Rock is a spectacular rocky island in the North Sea, renowned for its birdlifePhotograph: Sandy Gilmour/Siena international photo awards 2026

Sea Lion Games (Champion Islet, Galápagos Islands, Ecuador)

Journeys and adventures, third place: Guardian of the Cattle (South Sudan)

Documentary and photojournalism, highly commended: Massacre (Kostiantynivka, Ukraine)

The beauty of nature, commended: The Tree of Iceland

Street photography, commended: Flyboarding (Musandam, Oman)

Underwater life, winner: Commotion in the Ocean (Shetland Islands, UK)

Sports in action, highly commended: Sun Shadow Skater (Bolzano, Italy)

Documentary and photojournalism, commended: Jimmy Carter Lies in State at Dusk (Washington DC)

Documentary and photojournalism, highly commended: Surviving in the Shadows (Gaza, Palestine)

Sports in action, second place: The Dark Knight (Teahupo’o, Tahiti)

Animals in their environment, winner: Power Play (Torres del Paine national park, Magallanes, Chile)

Fascinating faces and characters, highly commended: Julien (Damascus, Syria)

Under-20, commended: Wunderpus Octopus (Anilao, Philippines)

The beauty of nature, third place: The Sporologist (France)

Lycoperdon pyriforme ), a saprophytic fungus with a distinctive pear-shaped form, takes place under the silent gaze of a small woodland snail slowly climbing across its surface. The puffball relies on the dispersal of spores produced inside the gleba, which, when mature, are released through a small apical pore. When the fruiting body is stimulated by external factors such as rain or the passage of animals, the spores are expelled in a thin cloud, resembling smoke, which is carried by the wind, ensuring the continuity of the species’ life cyclePhotograph: Benjamin Pawlica/Siena international photo awards 2026

Fascinating faces and characters, highly commended: The Barefoot Volcanologist (Tanna, Vanuatu)

Underwater life, highly commended: Expectant Parents (Anilao, Philippines)

Street photography, second place: The Fan Out (London, UK)

Street photography, highly commended: The Trousers Man (Varanasi, India)

Journey and adventures, highly commended: Pickering Hotel 4 (Singapore)

Exhibition: Witness to Our Time – James Nachtwey

Journeys and adventures, commended: In One Line

Photographer of the year: Amina (Kabul, Afghanistan)

article_text:
It’s not every day that the art world gets a public break-up, but that’s the case with art collective MSCHF . This week, cofounder and founding chief creative officer Lukas Bentel announced, via a formal press release, he was leaving the group to pursue solo work.

“I am enormously grateful and proud of the MSCHF team and what we created together, it was an enormous collective effort,” Bentel said in a statement. “We moved athletically at MSCHF, but we were designing stories that last. That’s where I want to get back to: making art that stays with people long after the moment has passed.”

Since its founding in 2019, MSCHF has made a name for itself via a series of viral artworks that often take aim at the excesses of the art world. They range from Severed Spots (2020), for which they purchased of a Damien Hirst “Spot” painting for $30,485 which the collective then sold each spot for $450 apiece to ATM Leaderboard , a project for the 2022 edition of Art Basel Miami Beach in which visitors could swipe their card and have their checking balance visible on the screen (ranked). At one point, the top spot was held by someone with $9.5 million in an account.

“Contemporary art feels increasingly irrelevant because it is siloed in the walls of a gallery or museum. We wanted to make work that was in the world, that was consumed as a product and engaged with culture,” Bentel said of the collective.

More recently, MSCHF has garnered art world acceptance, including representation with Perrotin. In 2024, they staged three shows with the gallery at its spaces in Seoul, Los Angeles, and New York. The latter one involved slowly taking parts of a bathroom sink at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and reconstructing it at the gallery for Met’s Sink Of Theseus .

The press release adds that Bentel “conceived, designed, created or directed nearly 300 released works at MSCHF spanning sculpture, footwear, fashion, software, publishing, furniture and vehicles.” Other projects by the group include the creation of a pair of viral Big Red Boots that flooded social media to the saving of a two-year-old cow from being slaughter. Last year, Phaidon published Made by MSCHF , which documented its first six years.

While Bentel pursues “solo art projects as well as commissioned design and commercial work,” it seems like MSCHF is still going forward with some of its Daniel Greenberg, Stephen Tetreault, Gabriel Whaley, and Kevin Wiesner. Its website lists 125 projects with a series of question marks for projects 126–135. But as with any band break-up, the question that remains is, Will the group be the same without one of its founder?
excerpt_original: He said he wants to get back to “making art that stays with people long after the moment has passed.”

article_text:
News

Karachi Biennale 2027 Canceled Due to War Conditions

The Karachi Biennale has canceled its fifth edition, originally scheduled to take place across the Pakistani port city from January 16–31, 2027. In an announcement released on October 9 via Instagram and its website, organizers attributed the decision to “war conditions prevailing in the region and the resultant logistical constraints and incertitude.”

Curated by art historian and researcher Noor Ahmed, the fifth iteration was organized under the dual Urdu and English title “Kal (Yesterday/Tomorrow).” Following the announcement, Ahmed told Pakistani outlet Dawn that the cancelation was a “unilateral” decision made without her prior consultation. Ahmed, who also spoke with Hyperallergic, noted that artists and collaborators had expressed dismay over “how communications and commitments . . . are being handled.” Over the course of 13 months, she had assembled over 100 artists and creative practitioners alongside three co-curators—two international and one based in Pakistan.

Since its inaugural exhibition in 2017, the Karachi Biennale has served as the flagship project of the Karachi Biennale Trust, establishing itself as Pakistan’s largest contemporary art platform. Over the past decade, the organization reports engaging 841 artists from across 50 countries, drawing approximately 50,000 in-person visitors alongside a substantial global digital audience.

The Karachi Biennale 2027 was conceived around the metaphor of an urban archipelago—a convergence of habitats, myths, and inventions where historical sediment mingles with future horizons.

At present, Karachi remains poised between crisis and reinvention. Its ecological fragility—manifested in suffocating mangroves, rising sea levels, and polluted waters—coexists with the pressures of uncontrolled urbanization, sectarian and ethnic conflicts, and the contentious memories surrounding its identity.

Yixuan Zhang is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.

article_text:
Chabe! magazine has announced the publication of its next issue.

This new edition, due to be published mid-December 2026, will showcase 22 emerging talents and seasoned photographers offering diverse perspectives on the world and Lyon, brought together in a beautiful 112-page booklet. Against a backdrop of significant pressures on cultural organisations and independent media, our commitment remains unchanged: high-quality content, and an engaged community. Every year for the past five years, Chabe! has produced an annual print magazine, followed by a year-round programme of cultural events centred on photographers: exhibitions, talks, events and artistic collaborations. In 2025, Chabe! was awarded the Grand Prix du Patrimoine for its work promoting Lyon’s cultural heritage. Friends, supporters, photographers, image enthusiasts and anyone keen to join a committed community: sign up to support the launch of Issue number 5!

article_text:
Vasyl Cherepanyn has titled his edition of the Berlin Biennale Central Europe Eastern Time . Opening in June 2027 and taking place across venues including KW Institute for Contemporary Art and the Hamburger Bahnhof – Nationalgalerie der Gegenwart, the show ‘proposes a new reading of Berlin from the East and offers a perspective on Europe shaped by those regions, experiences, and societal realities that have long been pushed to the margins of the European narrative. The title serves as a navigation tool, an instrument of orientation.’

The Ukrainian curator says he hopes to expand ‘upon the spatial and temporal coordinates already inscribed in the name of the Berlin Biennale and places the city within a broader Eastern European context, stretching from the Balkans to the Baltics, from Central Europe to the South Caucasus and beyond.’

The biennale is in its fourteenth edition.

Cherepanyn was born in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, and currently lives in Berlin. He is the cofounder and head of the Visual Culture Research Center (VCRC), which organises the Kyiv Biennial, and is a founding member of the East Europe Biennial Alliance.

Deze week is Menko Dijksterhuis te gast bij Kunst is Lang. Menko is een mixed media kunstenaar die met zijn werk maatschappelijke structuren kritisch bevraagt. Hij zet er een mogelijke toekomst tegenover waarin queer en gehandicapte lichamen worden omarmd en gevierd. Zijn werk komt veelal tot stand met analoge technieken, een proces en medium dat Menko ziet als metafoor voor zijn CRIP-bestaan.

De reeks Fuck Disabled People bestaat uit zwart-witte foto’s van Menko in intieme poses met een andere man. En zijn recente performance HOMO OBSCURA baseerde hij op een medisch video-archief van een Belgische neuroloog, die aan het begin van de 20e eeuw mensen diagnosticeerde via video-opnames. Menko neemt naakt, met een camera op hem gericht die zijn beeld live op een scherm projecteert, de poses aan die op de historische röntgenfoto’s te zien zijn.

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“ Whalefall ” is an undersea thriller that would like to do for whales what “Jaws” did for sharks. But it doesn’t work out that way. The movie comes closer to doing for whales what “Howard the Duck” did for barnyard superheroes — it makes you never want to see one of them again. Whales, of course, are beautiful creatures, and the one in “Whalefall” is a sperm whale with the boxy shape of a submarine, long and angular, a sleekly gliding beast that rules the ocean. article_text:
“ Whalefall ” is an undersea thriller that would like to do for whales what “Jaws” did for sharks. But it doesn’t work out that way. The movie comes closer to doing for whales what “Howard the Duck” did for barnyard superheroes — it makes you never want to see one of them again. Whales, of course, are beautiful creatures, and the one in “Whalefall” is a sperm whale with the boxy shape of a submarine, long and angular, a sleekly gliding beast that rules the ocean. Yet for most of the movie, we’re inside that whale. Literally inside it. The central character, Jay Gardiner ( Austin Abrams ), has gone scuba diving off the coast of Monastery Beach near Monterey, Ca., in search of the body of his father, a gruff seaman who committed suicide. (He had mesothelioma, a form of cancer that meant he couldn’t dive anymore; for him, that meant life was no longer worth living.)

Related Stories

'Amanda the Adventurer' Video Game Movie Adaptation in the Works From Blumhouse, MatPat and Epic Pictures

Jason Blum on How ‘Other Mommy’ Got That Controversial Title, Kristen Bell Joins ‘Violent Night 2’ and More From Blumhouse at NYCC

After submerging himself, Jay gets entangled in the tentacles of a giant squid, and that’s when the whale, who feeds on squid, pulls both Jay and the squid into his oversize gaping mouth. Moments later, Jay is trapped inside, surrounded by gooey protrusions of undulating flesh. For the rest of the movie, he’ll attempt to survive inside that whale, and to free himself before his oxygen runs out, which means keeping himself from getting sucked out of the creature’s digestive antechamber (which glows phosphorescent blue) and into its inner stomach cavity (which glows a hellish red), where the stomach acid will start to dissolve him.

For a moment, it occurred to me that Jay might run into his father, à la Jonah or Geppetto. But no, he’s on his own, doing all he can to escape this tight squeeze of whale flesh. Is it gross? At times. Claustrophobic? A bit. Scary? Not even a little. The place Jay finds himself looks like a colonoscopy designed by H.R. Giger. The visual effects are…okay. At times, it’s as if we were locked in some pop-up theme-park ride called Full Cavity Search. At one point, Jay uses a jellyfish the whale has eaten to light his way, and that’s as close as he comes to finding a companion. “Whalefall” is a fearless tale of human perseverance and mammalian stomach lining. It should have been called “Project Hail Fish Guts.”

Watching “Whalefall,” I kept thinking, “Why would anyone want to see this movie?” But the answer is obvious. “Whalefall” was adapted from Daniel Kraus’s 2023 novel, which in addition to being a bestseller was greeted with a great deal of acclaim. But something got lost in the translation. The thuddingly literal-minded movie that director Brian Duffield has made of it is a piece of thriller kitsch, full of unintentional laughs. With a hero who spends the heart of the film sucking on his oxygen mouthpiece, not so much talking as making frantic grunts of fear, “Whalefall” shuts us off from the most basic rooting interest. Sure, we want to see Jay get the hell out of there, but only because the whole ordeal is so stultifying and unpleasant.

It’s saying something that this is the second movie in a month where Austin Abrams has to fight his way out of the grip of fleshy tentacles, and only one of those movies isn’t terminally preposterous, and that’s “Resident Evil.” Abrams had an indie-hipster-on-the-run appeal in Zach Cregger’s horror hit, but in “Whalefall” he’s too wimpy by half, a simpering college kid who never proves to the audience that he has the right stuff. The film, like the book, takes off from the troubled relationship between Jay and his father, Mitt, played by Josh Brolin with a mean glare and body tattoos, in one of those brusquely overstated performances as an abusive macho dad — a Not So Great Santini who thinks the best way to prepare his son for what a tough world it is out there is to make the kid hate and respect him, in that order. As Brolin plays him, Mitt is like Robert Shaw’s Quint in “Jaws,” only ratcheted up several notches of boozy psycho masochism.

The film keeps jumping to flashbacks of Jay and Mitt at different points in their relationship, which is basically one long downhill slide. By the second half, though, Jay starts to realize that Mitt has actually taught him everything he needs to know to free himself from his predicament. The message? The young man who bonds with the ghost of his a–hole father while trapped in a gooey cushion of whale intestines stays with the ghost of his a–hole father. “Whalefall” even has an “ecological” side: The title refers to what happens when a whale’s carcass sinks to the ocean floor, an event that can give rise to a rich marine ecosystem. But “Whalefall,” the movie, is a carcass of a thriller that never rises.

article_text:
写真家・グラフィックデザイナーの横澤進一による個展「FORKTAIL」が、2026年10月31日（土）から11月24日（火）まで、京都・西陣の写真ギャラリー「芥 Aquta」で開催される。

本展では、横澤の出身地である埼玉と、現在暮らす東京で撮影した風景写真を展示。さらに、家屋や車、河川、猫、墓など、身近なモチーフを題材にセルフパブリッシングで制作してきた写真集も紹介する。

長年グラフィックデザインの仕事に携わってきた横澤は、2006年頃から写真撮影とZINE、写真集の制作を開始。クライアントのためにデザインする仕事とは異なり、自らが表現の主体となって写真を撮り、本をつくる活動を続けてきた。

街を歩き、視覚が反応した瞬間を写真に収め、それを一冊の本へと編集する。横澤は、写真とデザインという二つの視点を往復する制作について、「借り物でない私自身の万物との関わり方なのかもしれません」と語る。

会場の芥 Aqutaは、築約80年の旧西陣織工場を改装し、2025年に開館した写真ギャラリー。約6000冊の写真集を所蔵する空間で、横澤の写真と出版活動を横断的に紹介する。

タイトル

横澤進一「FORKTAIL」

場所

芥 Aquta（京都府京都市上京区笹屋町3丁目602-2）

会期

2026年10月31日（土）〜11月24日（火）

時間

12:00〜19:00

休み

水・木曜日

料金

1ドリンク制

URL

https://aquta.photo/

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "档案——2017年10月19日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴黎，大皇宫，1955年10月：DS19 在巴黎车展（Salon de l’Auto）亮相时赢得一片赞誉。“这款新雪铁龙引起轰动”，《十字架报》（La Croix）头条写道；“这是一颗炸弹”，《汽车杂志》（L’Auto Journal）宣称；“也许是火星人的车”，《法兰西星期日》（France-Dimanche）说。这款备受期待的车型由 Traction 和 2CV 发展而来，其创造者是负责该厂商研究部门的工程师安德烈·勒费弗尔（André Lefèbvre）和造型总监弗拉米尼奥·贝尔托尼（Flaminio Bertoni）——它本身就是一场盛事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "助力转向、液压传动、可调离地间隙的自调平液气悬挂……这一切都充满现代感，是创新的集中体现，其未来主义美学给当时的汽车生产投下一颗炸弹：车头比车尾更宽，发动机盖向下倾斜，散热格栅极简，塑料车顶两侧配有锥形闪烁转向灯，车身颜色表则邀人远行：巴拿马黄、东方蓝、里约红、坎大哈灰。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这套书献给那些因备受珍爱而成为传奇的汽车。不是高不可攀的，不是时髦的、傲慢的魔鬼美人，而是真诚而忠诚的朋友，其天然魅力永远锁在心底……这些不可替代之物神秘地继续散发着那个时代的气息，重现那个时代的色彩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "每一本都是一册此前未见的照片集，从无名家庭的鞋盒里发掘出来，是或多或少构图不佳的纪念照，却十分珍贵：这些“来自生活”的照片，是在汽车自身环境中的快照，是日常使用的汽车，没有为“官方”照片化上的妆，也没有为商业目的摆出的姿态。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在真实生活中发现 DS——它住在哪里、和谁一起出门、行驶在哪些道路上——揭示了当时的汽车在多大程度上被视为家庭的一员，在照片中无处不在，被邀请参加最简朴的野餐、每一场婚礼，是所有旅行的伙伴，是假期中不可避免的同谋。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管有数字技术的便利及其免费像素，今天却很难确定，汽车还会被如此频繁、如此温柔地拍摄，会被自发地邀请“入镜”，并自然地与生活中的小小乐趣联系在一起——这些乐趣在当时被认为值得铭记……汇编一份温情脉脉的幸福时光记录，也显示了这些留存下来的影像的价值。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《雪铁龙 DS》 由 This Is Not A Map 出版 9.90€", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "http://www.thisisnotamap.com/", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Archives – October 19, 2017

Paris, Grand Palais, October 1955: a salvo of praise greets the presentation of the DS19 at the Salon de l’Auto . “ The new Citroën is a sensation ”, headlines La Croix , “ This is the bomb ”, announces L’Auto Journal , “ Perhaps it’s the Martians’ car ” says France-Dimanche . Developed from the Traction and the 2CV by its creators – the engineer André Lefèbvre, in charge of the constructor’s research department, and Flaminio Bertoni, its styling director – this highly-anticipated model is the event.

Power-assisted steering, hydraulic transmission, self-levelling hydro-pneumatic suspension with adjustable ground clearance… Everything is modern in this concentration of innovations whose futuristic aesthetic puts a bomb under the production of the day: a prow wider than the stern, a plunging bonnet, a minimalist radiator grill, a plastic roof flanked by tapered, flashing turn-indicators and a bodywork colour chart that invites you to travel: Panama Yellow, Orient Blue, Rio Red, Kandahar Grey.

This collection of books is devoted to the cars that were so cherished as to become mythical. Not the inaccessible, not the fashionable, arrogant beauties of the devil, but the sincere and loyal friends whose natural charm is forever locked in the heart… These irreplaceables that mysteriously continue to exude the perfume of the period and revive the colour of the times.

Each one is an album of previously unseen photos, exhumed from unknown families’ shoeboxes, souvenir photos more or less well-framed, but precious: pictures “from life”, snapshots in its environment, the everyday car, without the make-up put on for the “official” pictures and striking a pose for commercial purposes.

Discovering the DS in its real life – where it lives, who it goes out with, the roads it travels – reveals how much the car of that time is considered a member of the family, omnipresent in the photos, invited to the most modest picnic, to every wedding, partner of all the trips, inevitable accomplice of the holidays.

Despite the conveniences of digital technology and its free pixels, nothing is less certain today than that the car would be photographed so much and so tenderly, that it would be invited spontaneously “into the frame” and naturally associated with life’s small pleasures, judged at the time to be memorable… Putting together a tender-hearted record of happy days also shows the value of these surviving images.

Citroën DS Published by This Is Not A Map 9.90€

editorial_title_zh: 凯莉·克拉克森与发条鸟风波始末
editorial_excerpt_zh: 此外，还有一份令人困惑的文化界“自由思想者”名单、“包厘街：魔鬼英里”以及其他艺术界动态。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Artnet快报》（Artnet Bulletin）是我们每日精选的艺术界五条值得了解的内容。每天早晨由不同的作者轮流撰写。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "关于凯莉·克拉克森与一家布鲁克林魔术店纠纷的个人按语……", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "好吧，这是一件非常滑稽却又闹得很大的事情：“独立女杰”（Miss Independent）歌手凯莉·克拉克森（Kelly Clarkson）与布鲁克林一家小型魔术店“玩乐艺术”（Art of Play）在网络上陷入了激烈的争执，起因是她打听购买某件会唱歌的鸟类雕塑时，双方各执一词，一方认为对方店员态度粗鲁。说真的，去查查看吧。这可是桩大新闻。我在这里要说：我坚决支持“玩乐艺术”！它出售来自世界各地的精美益智玩具，而且我在后方书架后面的隐蔽剧场里看过了我这辈子最棒的魔术表演——由无可比拟的大卫·威廉姆森（David Williamson）呈现。我在那儿的时候，也顺便打听了那个魔术发条鸟雕塑，店主在每次表演前都会展示它。它是西雅图艺术家布利斯·科尔布（Bliss Kolb）的作品。由于我自己也来自西雅图，且父亲酷爱时钟和其他发条小玩意儿，我和克拉克森一样想了解更多细节，而且我必须说，店员当时显得有点守口如瓶。但我只是把这解读为他们在维持一种神秘感。这只鸟就像是这家店的吉祥物！整个店铺奇妙的地方就在于它感觉充满了秘密！", "links": [{"text": "Art of Play", "url": "https://www.artofplay.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4USWt3gDVINHK2GhYBF7GmIkglDl1r1EGPDnrsnswp60_4z0FBP"}, {"text": "Huge story", "url": "https://www.vulture.com/article/kelly-clarkson-brooklyn-game-store-feud.html"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "quote", "text": "查看 Instagram 上的这篇帖子：Art of Play (@artofplay) 发布的一篇帖子", "links": [{"text": "A post shared by Art of Play (@artofplay)", "url": "https://www.instagram.com/p/DeXYsDaD8ja/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "文化界“自由思想者”的随性名单……", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出于某种原因，在其创刊40周年之际，《独立报》发布了“独立报自由思想者名单”，其中收录了在该报创刊期间“展现出自由思想”的人物。入选的40位自由思想者包括艺术家艾未未（“改变了政治参与型当代艺术的可能性”）和翠西·艾敏（“使忏悔、脆弱和自传成为当代艺术合法的主题”）。这些选择并不完全象征着“激进的自由思想”；它们相当家喻户晓。该名单中其余的大杂烩还包括维吉尔·阿布洛（Virgil Abloh）、理查德·道金斯（Richard Dawkins）、邓小平、埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）、珊达·瑞姆斯（Shonda Rhimes）、玛格丽特·撒切尔（Margaret Thatcher）和唐纳德·J·特朗普（Donald J. Trump）。真让人摸不着头脑。", "links": [{"text": "dropped", "url": "https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/independent-thinking/free-thinkers-stephen-hawking-elon-musk-b3062073.html"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "关于马克·费舍尔的第二种意见……", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "已故理论家、《资本主义现实主义》（Capitalist Realism，2009）的作者马克·费舍尔（Mark Fisher），在艺术写作界依然是主要的理论参考之一，而艺术写作界在很大程度上已经用态度取代了理论。作家兼研究员罗穆洛·莫赖斯（Rômulo Moraes）在他的博客 Ear Vortex 上发表了一篇充满态度和理论色彩的尖锐异议。一句话总结就是：费舍尔是“虚假紧迫感以及从他人更优秀作品中抄袭并调整过时思考过程的制造者”。我恰好同意费舍尔的文化悲观主义已经过了保质期，被重新加工成了诸如W·大卫·马克思（W. "不容错过的展览……", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“包厘街：魔鬼英里”（“The Bowery: Devil’s Mile”）是新美术馆（New Museum）里一个出人意料的广受欢迎的展览，千万不要淹没在与它同时开幕的亚瑟·杰法（Arthur A different writer takes over each morning."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "A Personal Note Re: Kelly Clarkson’s Feud With a Brooklyn Magic Shop…"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "OK, here’s a very silly but very big story: “Miss Independent” singer Kelly Clarkson is in a furious internet dispute with tiny Brooklyn magic shop the Art of Play over whether or not its staff was rude to her when she inquired about buying a certain singing bird sculpture. Seriously, look it up. Huge story . I’m here to say: I’m team Art of Play all the way. It sells incredible puzzles sourced from around the world, and I saw the best magic show of my life—by the incomparable David Williamson —in the hidden theater behind the bookshelf in the back. While I was there, I also happened to ask about the magic wind-up bird sculpture, which the owners show off before each performance. It’s by an artist named Bliss Kolb from Seattle. Being from Seattle myself and having a dad who loves clocks and other wind-up gizmos, I also, like Clarkson, wanted more details, and I will say the staff seemed mildly cagey. But I simply interpreted this as them maintaining an air of mystery. The bird in question is like the mascot for the store! And the entire wonder of the store is that it feels full of secrets!", "links": [{"text": "Art of Play", "url": "https://www.artofplay.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4USWt3gDVINHK2GhYBF7GmIkglDl1r1EGPDnrsnswp60_4z0FBP"}, {"text": "Huge story", "url": "https://www.vulture.com/article/kelly-clarkson-brooklyn-game-store-feud.html"}]}, {"type": "quote", "text": "View this post on Instagram A post shared by Art of Play (@artofplay)", "links": [{"text": "A post shared by Art of Play (@artofplay)", "url": "https://www.instagram.com/p/DeXYsDaD8ja/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "A Random List of Culture’s ‘Free Thinkers’…"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For some reason, for its 40th birthday, the Independent has dropped the “Independent’s Free Thinkers List,” featuring “people who have exhibited free thinking” during the paper’s lifetime. The 40 chosen Free Thinkers include artists Ai Weiwei (“changing the possibilities of politically engaged contemporary art“) and Tracey Emin (“helped make confession, vulnerability and autobiography legitimate subjects for contemporary art”). These picks do not exactly symbolize “radical free-thinking”; they are pretty familiar. The rest of the list’s grab bag includes the likes of Virgil Abloh , Richard Dawkins , Deng Xiaoping , Elon Musk , Shonda Rhimes , Margaret Thatcher , and Donald J. Trump .
